figure: FIGURE 11.3, panel A (Within one NVLink domain)
issue: The printed per-request on-node transfer time (0.08 s) is inconsistent with the figure's own 4-GPU prefill / 4-GPU decode grids and the 'per GPU' rate label. The top line reads '~35 GB ≈ 0.08 s' and the link is labeled '450 GB/s per GPU per direction', but 0.08 s = 35/450 treats the full 35 GB as traversing a single 450 GB/s link. With 4 prefill GPUs and 4 decode GPUs (TP sharding, which is mandatory for the canonical 70B since 140 GB > 80 GB per GPU), the 35 GB KV is split 4 ways and the 4 GPU-pair links run in parallel, so the per-request transfer latency is 35/(4·450) = 8.75/450 ≈ 0.02 s, i.e. 4× smaller than printed. Note 11.3-1 (p.190) repeats the single-link arithmetic: 'at NVLink's 450 GB/s per direction (§9.2) that transfer is 35 ÷ 450 ≈ 0.08 s'.
evidence: Panel A shows a 2×2 orange grid under 'PREFILL / 4 GPUs' and a 2×2 blue grid under 'DECODE / 4 GPUs'; link label '450 GB/s per GPU per direction'; header line '~35 GB ≈ 0.08 s (on-node, unidirectional)'. 35/450 = 0.0778 s (printed), but 35/(4·450) = 0.0194 s (implied by the 4 parallel GPU-pair links). The DP=4 reading that would justify 35 GB per link is infeasible for 70B (140 GB weights cannot replicate onto 80 GB GPUs).
acceptance_test: The printed on-node per-request time must equal 35 GB divided by the aggregate prefill→decode bandwidth implied by the depicted GPU count and per-GPU rate (≈0.02 s for 4 GPU pairs), OR the figure/note must explicitly state that 0.08 s is a single-unsharded-link conservative bound. The 'per GPU' label, the 4+4 GPU grids, and the 0.08 s figure must be mutually consistent; the same fix must be applied to Note 11.3-1 on p.190.

issue: The header 'A. Within one NVLink 4 domain' contains a stray '4' that is ambiguous (4th-generation NVLink vs a 4-GPU NVLink domain) and contradicts the '8× H100 host' box drawn directly beneath it (8 GPUs, not 4). The rest of the book refers to the on-node fabric simply as 'NVLink' (Fig 10.1, p.172: 'on-node in the canonical config (NVLink)'; p.179: 'NVLink 900 GB/s is aggregate peak'), so 'NVLink 4' is also a terminology outlier. A reader who parses '4' as a GPU count sees a 4-GPU domain header sitting on an 8-GPU host.
evidence: Header text 'A. Within one NVLink 4 domain' vs the gray box label '8× H100 host' containing 4+4 GPU grids; p.172 caption 'on-node in the canonical config (NVLink)'; p.179 'NVLink 900 GB/s is aggregate peak'.
acceptance_test: The panel-A header names the on-node interconnect without a '4' that conflicts with the 8-GPU host depicted, and matches the book's elsewhere-just-'NVLink' usage (e.g. 'within one NVLink (NVSwitch) domain' or 'on-node (NVSwitch)').

issue: The subtitle 'the split is the same; the transfer link — and its cost — is not' sits above two panels whose per-side GPU counts differ (panel A: 4+4 GPUs; panel B: 8+8 GPUs). 'The split is the same' most naturally reads as the prefill/decode separation being identical, but a reader comparing the panels sees different GPU partitions and may conclude the figure contradicts its own subtitle.
evidence: Panel A labels 'PREFILL / 4 GPUs' and 'DECODE / 4 GPUs'; panel B labels 'PREFILL / 8× H100 host' and 'DECODE / 8× H100 host'; subtitle 'the split is the same; the transfer link — and its cost — is not'.
acceptance_test: A reader cannot infer from the subtitle that the per-side GPU partition is identical when the panels visibly show 4 vs 8 GPUs; the subtitle should specify that 'split' refers to the prefill/decode separation (the architectural P/D split), not the per-side GPU count.

issue: The caveat line 'Per-request times assume an unshared per-GPU link; 1.4 TB/s exceeds any single link above' uses the unit 'per-GPU link', but panel B's link is labeled '40 GB/s per host NIC' — a host-level, not GPU-level, unit. The caveat's unit therefore does not match panel B.
evidence: Caveat text 'Per-request times assume an unshared per-GPU link' vs panel B link label '40 GB/s per host NIC' (and panel A label '450 GB/s per GPU per direction').
acceptance_test: The caveat's link unit matches the unit shown in each panel (e.g. 'an unshared dedicated link — per-GPU in A, per-host NIC in B'), so the 'exceeds any single link above' check is stated in the same units the panels use.
